title: Fixing Redis Fork Copy-on-Write Memory Bloat
prompt: A production Redis 7 primary holds a 24 GB dataset on a 32 GB RAM Linux host and handles 15,000 writes/sec (each mutating ~64 bytes across random keys). Whenever an hourly `BGSAVE` RDB snapshot (taking 90 seconds) or `BGREWRITEAOF` triggers `fork()`, the child process shares pages with the parent via Copy-on-Write (CoW). Within 70 seconds of `fork()`, Redis RSS balloons from 24 GB to >31.5 GB and the Linux kernel OOM-kills the Redis primary. Inspection shows Transparent Huge Pages (THP) is set to `always`. Design the OS memory, Redis persistence, and automated CoW-guardrail architecture to prevent OOM kills while preserving durable backups.

spark.summary: When Linux Transparent Huge Pages (2 MB) is enabled, a 64-byte write during Redis BGSAVE fork() copies an entire 2 MB page (512x write amplification), doubling RSS from 24 GB to 48 GB in 90 seconds and triggering the OOM killer.
spark.keyTakeaway: When Redis runs `BGSAVE` or `BGREWRITEAOF`, `fork()` shares memory pages with the child via Copy-on-Write (CoW), disable Transparent Huge Pages (`echo never > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled`), cap Redis `maxmemory` at <= 55% of host RAM, monitor `rdb_last_cow_size`, and gate BGSAVE during heavy write bursts.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** When Redis runs `BGSAVE` or `BGREWRITEAOF`, `fork()` shares memory pages with the child via Copy-on-Write (CoW). Under standard `4 KB` Linux pages, `15,000` random 64-byte writes/sec over 90s dirties at most `~5.4 GB`.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts 2 MB Hugepages Turn 24 GB BGSAVE into OOM Kill in 70s (15k Writes/s -> Redis Primary (24GB) -> Linux CoW + THP -> BGSAVE Child); THP=never (4 KB CoW) + Replica Snapshot Offload (15k Random Writes/s -> Primary (maxmemory <=55%) -> Async Replication Stream -> Backup Replica (BGSAVE)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Running a `fork()`-enabled Redis primary at `75%–85%` of host RAM leaves less than `25%` headroom for normal `4 KB` CoW overhead, replica output buffers, and jemalloc fragmentation. Guarantee `used_memory + CoW_overhead <= 85%` of 32 GB RAM during 90-second snapshots: **Permanently Disable THP**: Set `transparent_hugepage=never` in kernel boot args / systemd.

**Failure Modes & Application:** OS page-table and CoW mechanics apply to all fork-based persistence engines: **Production Redis / Valkey Clusters**: Standardize `THP=never`, `vm.overcommit_memory=1`, and `50–55%` memory caps.
